=== Original heirship review — 30 October 2026 ===
The existing father [[Glascow-14|Isaac Glasgow]] is now assessed at '''94% confident inference''', superseding the earlier 83% grade. The original 1851 Weakley deed calls its grantors the heirs of deceased Isaac Glasgow and conveys land originally surveyed in his name. The one W.P.M. heir fits this distinctive name and family. Glasgow-116 and Glasgow-2613 have the same recorded 22 June 1829 birth and 1910 death and remain possible duplicate accounts of that one heir; no second son or merge is asserted. Numerous other heirs match Isaac’s existing family, including Elijah, William C., Wagstaff K., John G., Joseph D. and Jesse Glasgow, with the Adams couple. This supports confident fatherhood by the combined specific family group, rather than a generic same-name or age match.<ref name="WeakleyHeirs1851">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSKJ-RS12-5 Weakley County Register of Deeds, pp. 410–411], DGS 008151469, image 213; deed 20 February 1851, acknowledgment 14 March, registered 15 March. Original inspected 30 October 2026.</ref>

The record directly states heirship, not a literal child clause. Husbands are among the grantors and are not treated as biological children. This is a profile-specific confident inference; full middle names, vital dates, mothers and upstream ancestry are not proved by the deed. The one W.P.M. heir fits this distinctive name and family.
